venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU
dek: They ran it until FAU sat. They threw it now when the corners backed up. They took the ball when he held it.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — condensed draft for Charles. Fan rail stays empty.
headline: Florida did not trick FAU. They handed it to Baugh, they threw the hitch when the corners sat, and they waited for Veltkamp to hold it. The score is 66–21. The night is that simple.

offense.body:
Florida’s first snap of the Sumrall era is first-and-10 from their own 6, 12:00 left in the first. Philo in the shotgun. Baugh next to him. One tight end, three receivers. They huddle. They line up. They give it to Baugh. Nine yards. Faulkner’s first answer is not a shot play. It is the best player, downhill, after they have already spread you out.

Baugh already knows this offense. He does not wait on a crease to announce itself. At 7:17 the hole dies and he plants and bounces 18. In the third, third-and-2 at the Florida 33, they sit for him and he is gone 61 yards to the 6. He scores from 12 on a backside cut and from 7 with the pad down. Twenty-five snaps. One hundred sixty yards. That is not a feature back they sprinkled in. That is the play.

The line made that play legal. They moved people on the give and they held long enough for the quick game to be on time. Harris is the left guard in that group. Lovett, Moore, Shanahan, Ugorji are the rest of the first five. When the front clogged, Baugh still had a bounce. When it opened, he was already through it. Condensed will not let you grade every hand fight. It will let you see that the run did not die on first contact.

Philo’s job was to operate it, not to invent it. Two minutes after the first give they are at their own 23 and the picture has not changed. Corners sitting off. Hitch to Brown, eight yards, on time. After they drop him, he comes right back: Wilson, short left, 19 yards, first down. Stay on the field. Come back to the run. He is in and out of the read before the second level can close the window. That is the whole passing game on this tape until they make him hold it.

The snap that explains the night is first-and-10 at the FAU 49 with 8:49 left in the first. Same 11. Baugh on Philo’s left. Three receivers to the field, one to the boundary. The tight end is split out in the trips. FAU is in two-high and the corners are eight yards off. If they bring a body into the box, Baugh has the give. They do not. They sit. So Philo throws the hitch to Brown. Catch at the 50. First man misses. Brown runs 49 yards and the Swamp has its first touchdown of the year.

People will remember the score. The play is the throw. Five yards, on time, after they refused the run. Brown is in that window because he makes the first miss. Forty snaps. The 33-yard ball over the top later is the same idea with more air. That is who number 1 is on this tape. He turns a rhythm throw into a stadium play.

The skill guys finished the edges so that run and that hitch could be the same family. Stockton catches it short right and gets what is there. The tight ends are not standing around on the give. Abrams’ 63 only exists because the safety finally cheated Baugh — extra bodies stay in, second-and-6 from the Florida 29, 13:22 of the second, and Abrams runs by everybody down the right sideline. Faulkner does not open the night hunting that. He takes the lid off when they come down.

They did not live in a dropback. Shotgun. Run. Throw it now. Fourth-and-3 from the 3, 11:05 of the second, he empties the backfield. Five out. The ends climb. Contain is gone. Philo walks in. The keep is live because of how he lined them up, not because he called a gadget they hid all week.

When Baugh is off, Clark is the back. Twenty snaps. He runs like the play is his — downhill, no bounce-around, finish through the first man. Then the linebackers sit for that run, he releases, catch at the 4, he drives it in. The back becomes the receiver because they finally stopped the run with their eyes.

The other side of hitch is what happens when Philo holds it. Third-and-7 at the FAU 44, 44 seconds left in the half. The window is there and then it is not. Sweeney sits and takes it. The rhythm throw is this offense. When he waits, the play dies.

What Saturday was: stretch the field, hand it to Baugh, throw it now when they sit. Brown’s 49 is that throw. Abrams and the empty keep only exist because the run was real. Campbell will see the same picture. The question is whether they sit.
bullets: Baugh is the play. Downhill, bounce when it dies, gone when they sit.
Philo throws it now. When he holds it, Sweeney is sitting.
Brown’s 49 is a hitch and a miss — not a bomb.
They mixed the downhill give with the stretch. They did not live in a dropback.

defense.body:
White’s answer to a spread team that does not huddle is simple enough for fans and hard enough to play. Four down. Two linebackers. An extra defensive back on the slot. Corners off so nothing goes over their head. Rush four. Tackle the five-yard throw. Do not get cute.

They came downhill. That is the first thing you see even on the condensed cut. The front is not sitting and reading. Graham is in the picture on most of those snaps. Chiles is with him. When the rush shows, it is those two coming with the four, not a game they invented on third down.

The tax shows up on the first third down. FAU, shotgun, one back, 14:27 of the first, third-and-7 from their own 28. Corners are off. Veltkamp throws hitch to Henry. Ten yards. Converted. White will live with that throw if they tackle. That is the deal opening the night: give them the short one, go get the ball when it stays in the air.

The deal pays at 12:07. Third-and-10 at the Florida 35. Veltkamp in the gun, trips one side. White does not send the house. Four rush. Two safeties high. Everybody else drops. The ball comes out late. Coleman is already in the lane. He catches it at the 5 and the drive is over. Same idea, 4:01 of the second, first snap after Baugh scores, FAU at their own 25. Heat up the middle. Veltkamp throws off his back foot. Johnson goes up and gets it at the 30. Coleman is on the breakup. They gave up the hitch. They attacked the one he held.

They will pursue. They will tackle when the job is the job. They will also lose the ones you cannot lose in a phone booth. First-and-goal at the 1, 13:55 of the second. White packs the box. No bounce. Ervin still walks in. The front was right. They lost the pile.

The scramble is the other hole. Third-and-7 at the 7, 6:52 of the second. Same four-rush as Coleman’s pick. Veltkamp feels it, leaves, dives the pylon. Watch the end. His job is stay outside and keep the quarterback in. He does not. Same call. Different job lost. Contain. That is the hit they took on a night they otherwise ran to the ball.

Late in the third they fade you. First-and-10 at the Florida 20. Corners have been sitting off all night — that is the point of the defense. Valsin releases outside, stacks Flowers, wins the back line. Twenty-yard score. If you sit off to kill the deep ball, you have to win the fade when they throw it.

The front kept handing the job around. James is the end in that rotation. Lyons is one of the interior snaps they kept feeding. Bett is the one who finishes it. Fourth-and-1 at the 1 in the fourth, Veltkamp keeps left. Bett gets there. Ball out at the 5. Myles Johnson falls on it at the 11. The rush finally wins the one-on-one White had been waiting on.

What Saturday was: four down, extra DB on the slot, rush four, no deep ball. Coleman and Johnson are that plan. The sloppy part is the hitch they agreed to live with, plus the pile, the edge, and the fade. Campbell will throw the short one and run the quarterback. Same two jobs. Slot and the end who cannot leave.
bullets: They come downhill. Four rush, two-high. Make him hold it.
The hitch convert is the tax. Coleman and Johnson are the wait paying off.
The scramble and the pile are the jobs they lost.
Campbell: short throw and the quarterback run.

specials.body: Fourth-and-4 from the FAU 35, 2:10 left in the first. They can go for it. They let Durkin try it from 53 instead. Clean. 17–0, and Florida never punts. They took the points when the drive stalled and they never gave the ball back on fourth down the rest of the night.
bullets: Durkin from 53. They took the points.

keys: Baugh is the play. They run him until you sit. Then they throw it now.
Brown’s 49 is a hitch and a miss. Abrams and the empty keep only exist because the run was real.
White rushes four and waits. Coleman and Johnson are the wait. The scramble is the hole.
Campbell will throw hitch and run the quarterback. Same two jobs.

nextWeek.look: They will go fast and throw hitch. Faulkner will still run Baugh until they sit. White will still rush four. The snaps that matter are the short throw and whether the end stays home.
